documents.unit: Office of Educational Improvement, Faculty Development
documents.title: AI Digest | Teaching Toolbox
documents.summary: A faculty-development news digest from MCW's Office of Educational Improvement. It links external AI frameworks and resources, and summarizes a few MCW guiding principles (treat AI tools as public, protect data, verify and cite outputs, keep humans in judgement). It sets no course-level stance.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule of its own for AI in coursework; it is a digest of external resources and says program and course policies 'should be mindful of the institution's guiding principles', leaving course policy to programs and instructors, so delegates.

units.why: The page says 'MCW program and course policies should be mindful of the institution's guiding principles', a duty on programs and instructors writing course policy to align with the institutional framework, so P56 (institution-wide framework), modality should; P04 does not fit because it does not hand the decision over.
units.anchor: MCW program and course policies should be mindful of the institution’s guiding principles
units.frag_end: reviewed and updated on a regular basis.

units.why: The same sentence says the guiding principles 'are reviewed and updated on a regular basis', a statement of a review cycle, so P54 (revisit regularly) with modality informs.
units.anchor: which are reviewed and updated on a regular basis
units.frag_end: reviewed and updated on a regular basis.

units.why: The page points instructors to a 'crowdsourced spreadsheet of course-level policies for generative AI use to aid programs and instructors in developing their own policies', which is support for faculty setting policy, so P63 rather than P09; informs because it is a resource, not a rule.
units.anchor: crowdsourced spreadsheet of course-level policies for generative AI use
units.policy: Dr. Lance Eaton of Anchor Insights Consulting maintains and publishes a crowdsourced spreadsheet of course-level policies for generative AI use to aid programs and instructors in developing their own policies.
units.fit_note: The page links an external repository of example syllabus policies; it is a resource, not workshops or consultations.

units.why: The page says AAMC webinars with 'CME credit' help educators prepare AI integration in clinical education, a faculty-development offering, so P63 (support faculty in learning AI), informs.
units.anchor: AI Skill Building for Medical Educators
units.frag_end: CME credit is available for this webinar.
units.policy: The AAMC hosts an "AI Skill Building for Medical Educators" webinar series, and CME credit is available for the January 2026 session on AI integration into clinical education.

units.why: The AMA modules are described as 'a foundation for understanding that aids us in preparing our students to use AI in practice', offered free; this is AI-literacy training for the community, so P70; P44 was considered, but the act of the passage is offering modules.
units.anchor: free of charge and can provide a foundation for understanding
units.frag_start: These modules are free of charge
units.policy: The AMA ChangeMedEd modules on AI in health care are free of charge and provide a foundation for understanding that aids in preparing students to use AI in practice.
units.fit_note: Also states a professional-skill rationale (preparing students to use AI in practice, cf. P44).

units.why: The page recommends the ETHICAL framework: 'We encourage members of the MCW community to become familiar with this framework, apply it to their own use of AI', an institutional framework for responsible AI use, so P56 (not P02, since it encourages a framework, not AI use), modality should.
units.anchor: We encourage members of the MCW community to become familiar with this framework
units.frag_end: responsible use of AI in health sciences education.

units.why: The framework is named as 'a foundation for responsible AI use in higher education that is flexible and adaptable to a diverse array of circumstances', stating the purpose and scope of a principles framework, so P56 with modality informs.
units.anchor: foundation for responsible AI use in higher education that is flexible and adaptable

units.why: The InfoScope page 'provides a variety of resources to educate and support members of our institution on responsible, effective use of AI', which is institution-provided AI training and guides for the community, so P70 (not P63, because it is not faculty-only), informs.
units.anchor: resources to educate and support members of our institution on responsible, effective use of AI

units.why: The page says the InfoScope resources include 'Microsoft Co-Pilot information, recommendations, and tips and tricks', pointing to a licensed institutional assistant, so P17 (sanctioned tool) is the nearest type; it informs and does not require its use.
units.anchor: Microsoft Co-Pilot information, recommendations, and tips and tricks
units.policy: MCW's InfoScope page offers Microsoft Co-Pilot information, recommendations, and tips and tricks.
units.fit_note: Only says guidance on Co-Pilot is offered; it does not say Co-Pilot is the sanctioned or only tool.

units.why: MCW says its guiding principles are 'applicable to all faculty, staff, and students conducting MCW business in any of the four missions', a scope statement for the framework, so P56 with modality informs; P61 does not fit because it defines no term.
units.anchor: applicable to all faculty, staff, and students conducting MCW business

units.why: The page says 'The core of these principles is engaging in human-centered AI, with transparency being crucial', the guiding principle of the framework, so P56 with modality informs.
units.anchor: engaging in human-centered AI, with transparency being crucial to fostering open communication

units.why: The highlight 'In the absence of a formal contract, treat all AI tools as public' tells users to treat uncontracted tools as public, a data-protection and vetted-tool rule, so P50, modality must since it is an imperative.
units.anchor: In the absence of a formal contract, treat all AI tools as public.

units.why: 'Never enter protected information into a public AI model' is a flat ban on inputting protected data, so P50 (protect personal data) with must-not; P49 does not fit as it concerns course materials.
units.anchor: Never enter protected information into a public AI model.

units.why: 'Review AI outputs for accuracy and employ responsibility in its use' asks users to check AI output, so P31 (verify AI output), modality must as an imperative.
units.anchor: Review AI outputs for accuracy and employ responsibility in its use.

units.why: 'Cite AI outputs and use as appropriate' asks for citation of AI outputs, so P24 (disclose AI use), modality must as an imperative qualified by 'as appropriate'; P25 does not fit because no details are listed.
units.anchor: Cite AI outputs and use as appropriate.

units.why: 'AI is a tool and is not meant to replace human wisdom and judgement' states that AI must not replace human thinking, so P32 (stay the primary problem-solver) is the nearest type; informs because it is a principle.
units.anchor: AI is a tool and is not meant to replace human wisdom and judgement.
units.fit_note: Addressed to all users including staff and applies to human judgement generally, not only the student as problem-solver.

units.why: The page says the AAMC principles 'reflect the dynamic nature of the AI environment and will be updated as needed', a statement that the principles are provisional, so P54 (revisit regularly), informs.
units.policy: The AAMC principles for responsible use of AI in medical education reflect the dynamic nature of the AI environment and will be updated as needed.

documents.title: MCW All Student Policy Guide 2026
documents.summary: A university-wide student policy guide of about 123k characters. Its Academic Integrity section names AI-generated content in coursework as academic dishonesty; no other AI text appears.
documents.stance_why: The only AI statement lists 'Using artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate content for submitted coursework' among forms of academic dishonesty, with no exception, so AI generation of submitted work is banned: prohibit (limited to generating content).

units.why: The guide lists 'Using artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate content for submitted coursework' as academic dishonesty, so P36 (misconduct) is the type, because the sentence classifies the act as an integrity violation; P19 also fits but classification is the act of the sentence. must-not and prohibit since it bans the use.
units.anchor: Using artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate content for submitted coursework
units.fit_note: Also states the P19 rule (AI may not produce submitted work); unlike the neighbouring items, no faculty exception for AI is stated.

notes: Coder B. Student guide read around the Honor Code and Academic Integrity section; keyword searches (AI, artificial, generative, plagiarism, chatbot) found no other AI text. Third-party article summaries on the digest page (EdTech concerns, AAMC competencies and framework lists) were not coded as MCW policy.
